content.title: About
content.content: A crepe is a thin pancake made from a liquid batter of flour, eggs, milk, and a small amount of sugar. The batter spreads quickly on a hot pan, forming an almost translucent, flexible sheet that stays soft after cooling. Crepes are commonly served with a wide range of fillings – sweet (chocolate, fruit, whipped cream) or savory (cheese, ham, vegetables).

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Crepes originate from French cuisine, where they are called “crêpe”.
Because they cook in just a few seconds, crepes are popular at street fairs and festivals.
In Brittany, “Mardi Gras” is celebrated with sweet crepes sprinkled with sugar and lemon juice.
Crepes can be either sweet or savory depending on the batter additives and the chosen filling.
In some countries, such as Japan, similar thin pancakes called “okonomiyaki” are served with various toppings.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: The eggs in the batter provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Milk contributes calcium, which supports bone and dental health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Flour and eggs supply B1, B2, and B6 vitamins that aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When cooked with minimal oil, crepes are relatively low‑calorie compared with other pancakes.

items.title: Dietary flexibility
items.content: Recipes can be adapted with plant‑based milks or gluten‑free flours to meet specific dietary needs.

items.title: Egg or milk allergy
items.content: People allergic to eggs or dairy should avoid traditional crepes.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: Standard recipes use wheat flour, making crepes unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Crepes made from refined flour can cause rapid blood‑sugar spikes, so diabetics should watch portion size.

items.title: Over‑cooking
items.content: Burnt crepes may form acrylamide, a potentially harmful compound.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Crepes are served rolled or folded like an envelope with filling inside. Sweet versions include fruit compote, chocolate sauce, whipped cream, or powdered sugar. Savory versions feature ham, cheese, spinach, mushrooms, or a fried egg.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Freshly made crepes are best eaten immediately. If needed, store them in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a zip‑lock bag – they keep their softness for about a month. Before reheating, lightly dust with flour to prevent sticking.
